quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel semi-annual report: H1 FY2026 (11-11-2025)
quarterly_data.signal: First half to September 2025 (semi-annual report): revenue JPY 4,635.6 billion (prior-year half JPY 4,379.7 billion), business profit JPY 227.5 billion (JPY 375.7 billion) and a loss attributable to owners of the parent of JPY 113.3 billion (profit of JPY 243.3 billion a year earlier). By segment: Steelmaking revenue JPY 4,243.9 billion (JPY 3,990.5 billion), business profit JPY 201.8 billion (JPY 353.8 billion); Engineering JPY 182.2 billion (JPY 183.3 billion), profit JPY 7.4 billion (loss JPY 1.2 billion); Chemicals & Materials JPY 128.1 billion (JPY 140.4 billion), profit JPY 9.8 billion (JPY 12.2 billion); System Solutions JPY 179.0 billion (JPY 157.0 billion), profit JPY 17.5 billion (JPY 18.3 billion). Management describes the global steel business environment as an unprecedented crisis, with Chinese overproduction and exports structural and showing no sign of improvement and US tariffs, though lowered from the initial level, far higher than before; profit fell on worse production / shipments, margins (incl. FX) and inventory valuation. With the U.S. Steel merger completed in June 2025, Steelmaking segment headcount was 120,094 at September 30, 2025, up 23,381 from March 31, 2025. Half-year R&D spending was JPY 41.2 billion.

quarterly_data.quarter: Nippon Steel semi-annual report: H1 FY2026 (11-11-2025)
quarterly_data.signal: Chemicals & Materials in the first half (semi-annual report): at Nippon Steel Chemical & Material, the functional materials market was strong overall on AI-related demand and demand pulled forward by US tariff policy and Chinese subsidy policy; demand grew in particular for functional resins for high-speed communications, substrate materials for smartphones and semiconductor bonding wires on growing AI demand. Segment profit still fell amid high raw-material prices, China's weak economy and inventory adjustment of general-purpose semiconductors.
